   ITEM 3

  CITY OF ARTESIA

  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION AGENDA REPORT

DATE:  August 29, 2024

TO:  Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Adrian Fajardo, Management Analyst
FROM:  Melissa Burke, Deputy City Manager

SUBJECT:  Update on Climate Adaptation Planning Grant and the Artesia Climate
  Ready Program

BACKGROUND
On January 11, 2024, Staff brought an item before the Public Safety Commission to
discuss the City's application to the Sustainable Transportation – Climate Adaptation
Planning Grant.

On July 9, 2024, the City was notified that it had been awarded a grant of $342,036 for
the Artesia Climate Ready project. This project focuses on developing a comprehensive
Climate Action and Adaptation Plan (CAAP) to assess and adapt to the impacts of climate
change, particularly in enhancing the resilience of the City's transportation system against
extreme weather events like heatwaves, wildfires, and flooding.

ANALYSIS
In October, the City will solicit proposals for a consultant to develop the CAAP. The project
is anticipated to begin in November 2024 and is expected to be completed by June 2027.
During the project's Community Engagement and Drafting phases, Staff will actively seek
the Public Safety Commission's input, particularly in critical areas like evacuation
planning. The Commission's insights will ensure that the CAAP effectively addresses the
City's safety needs.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission receive and file an update on the
City's grant application to the Climate Adaptation Planning Program from the California
Department of Transportation.
   ITEM 4

  CITY OF ARTESIA

  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION AGENDA REPORT

DATE:  August 29, 2024

TO:  Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Adrian Fajardo, Management Analyst
FROM:  Melissa Burke, Deputy City Manager

SUBJECT:  Receive and File an Update on Automated License Plate Readers

BACKGROUND
In April 2024, the Public Safety Commission discussed the potential implementation of
Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) cameras throughout the City. This
discussion followed an increasing concern over vehicle-related crimes in Los Angeles
County, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance solutions to support public safety
efforts.

On May 13, 2024, the City Council approved a contract with Vigilant Solutions to deploy
ALPR cameras at critical intersections and thoroughfares within Artesia. These cameras
are intended to strengthen the City’s crime prevention and investigation capabilities by
capturing detailed vehicle data, including license plates, vehicle make, model, color, and
speed.

ANALYSIS
The project has encountered manufacturing and shipping delays, which have impacted
the installation timeline. However, progress has been made. Seven (7) of the eleven (11)
planned cameras have already been installed and are currently operational. The
remaining four cameras are expected to be installed by the beginning of September 2024.
Staff will continue to monitor the project's progress and effectiveness, providing updates
to the Public Safety Commission in future meetings.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission receive and file this update on the
implementation of Artesia’s Automated License Plate Readers
